clue.text: Mystery of blocked reserve

blocks.note: a blocked road or path is closed
to reserve a table or seat is to book it

explanation.surface: Someone puzzling over why the reserve stock has been blocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: The two wordplay words sit side by side, each giving one word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something or someone you cannot understand at all is idiomatically called a closed book.

clue.text: Bit of elegant gold instrument releasing cold alcohol

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is wanted, namely its opening letter
to release something is to let it go, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: the first letter of elegant
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an instrument is a device
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dainty gold gadget that dispenses chilled spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVICE loses its C to leave DEVIE; the phrase is French for 'water of life'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie is a clear fruit brandy, so it is a kind of distilled alcohol.

clue.text: Some frothy molecular substance used as antiseptic

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are needed, a run lying inside them

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A foaming chemical compound applied to clean wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join: fro(THY MOL)ecular.
explanation.definitionFit: Thymol is a compound from thyme oil that kills germs and appears in mouthwashes and disinfectants.

clue.text: Gutless idiot's bare bum

indicators.note: having no guts means losing the insides, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: a moron is an idiot

explanation.surface: A cowardly fool exposing his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: MORON loses its middle R. 'Gutless' reads as cowardly but strips the middle; the definition is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is slang for showing your naked buttocks to people as a prank or insult.

clue.text: Rituals upset nieces more

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and jumble it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Family rituals bother the nieces more than anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like it describes the nieces' feelings but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonies are formal ritual occasions, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Unusual pastry, split evenly by calorie

indicators.note: taking things evenly here means keeping only the letters in even-numbered positions
by means next to, so one piece is placed beside the other

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters across both words
cal is the standard abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: An odd pastry, cut evenly and served with its calorie count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' seems to describe cutting the pastry, but it is a source word too: the even letters run through both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, which is a direct synonym of unusual or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Argues over daughter and son getting weapons

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to row (rhyming with cow) is to argue
D is the abbreviation for daughter
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family quarrel over the children ends with everyone arming themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: ROW here is the British word for a quarrel, said to rhyme with cow; turned upwards it becomes SWOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Swords are bladed hand weapons, so they are a clear example of the general term.

clue.text: Impressionist art, featuring heavenly body

indicators.note: to feature something is to contain it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A painting by an Impressionist that shows a celestial object, as in Van Gogh's starry skies.
explanation.walkthrough: Look across the join: Impressioni(ST ART).
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a luminous ball of gas in the sky, one of the standard heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Awful Lothario initially promises to love setter

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Lothario
oaths are solemn promises
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A dreadful seducer swears undying love to the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lothario is a womaniser, which suits the surface; only his first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something hateful or repulsive, so it works as a stronger synonym for awful.

clue.text: In other words, pull with sex appeal

blocks.note: to tow a vehicle is to pull it
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Put plainly, pulling a partner is done with sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' tempts as British slang for attracting a partner, but here it is a plain haul. 'It' for sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is a formal phrase introducing a restatement or clarification, which is what 'that is' or 'namely' do.

clue.text: Second maiden playing as member of band

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A second young woman joins the line-up as a band member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' reads as making music, which fits the band, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideman is a supporting musician hired to play in a band, especially in jazz, rather than lead it.

clue.text: Heartless misjudgment by European politician and leader

indicators.note: with no heart the centre is lost, so the middle letter disappears

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an error is a misjudgment

explanation.surface: A cruel blunder by a European politician who also leads.
explanation.walkthrough: ERROR loses its central R; the European and the politician go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor rules an empire, so he is an example of a supreme leader or sovereign.

clue.text: Satan was revolting

indicators.note: revolting can mean turning round, as a wheel revolves, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: 'lived' as in existed, a sense of was

explanation.surface: The Devil was a disgusting figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting but means turning round; 'was' in the sense of existed gives the word to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the name of the chief evil spirit in Christian belief, who is called the Devil.

clue.text: Drives out cuts overwhelming soldiers

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: to excise is to cut out
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Military cutbacks, where reductions overwhelm the troops, push people out.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) for soldiers is a crossword staple; it sits inside EX-CISES.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to expel an evil spirit from a person or place, so it means to drive out.

clue.text: I loudly call for sign you're paying attention

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the pronoun and the organ of sight are said alike
to call someone is to contact them

explanation.surface: Someone shouting to get a sign that their listener is following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I loudly' sounds like shouting, but it means the letter I as heard, which is the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking someone in the eyes while they talk shows that you are listening and engaged.

clue.text: Group of players spreads spiteful gossip about extras

blocks.note: a team in sport is a side
to dish the dirt is to spread gossip

explanation.surface: A sports team badmouthing the film extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extras' suggests film walk-ons but here means additions to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Side dishes are served alongside the main course, as additions to it, so they are extras.

clue.text: Excessively focussed on one area, rewriting adverse policies

indicators.note: rewriting something produces a new version, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded government department redrafting harmful policies.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of the last two words rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overspecialised is to concentrate too narrowly on one field, which describes excessive focus.

clue.text: Mammals stamp on particles

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so one piece goes before the other

blocks.note: a seal is a stamp pressed into wax
ions are charged particles

explanation.surface: Animals trampling over tiny bits of matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' looks like a verb about trampling, but it is the noun for a wax seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lions are eared seals, marine animals that suckle their young, which makes them mammals.

clue.text: Gents swimming across river on Thursday, showing talent

indicators.note: swimming things move about freely, so the letters are mixed up
lying across something means spanning it, so one piece goes round another
in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first part comes before the next

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river
Th is the abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: Men swimming across a river on a Thursday, displaying their prowess.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranged GENTS becomes ST-ENG with the river inside, and the day's abbreviation goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A strength is something you are good at, so it can mean a talent or particular ability.

clue.text: Twist a short tournament for tropical tree-dwellers

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: a kink is a twist in a rope or hose
taken as written
a joust is a knightly tournament

explanation.surface: A twisted little contest put on for jungle animals.
explanation.walkthrough: JOUST loses its last letter. The answer is an unusual word, so build it from the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkajous are honey bears of Central and South American rainforests that live mostly in the canopy.

clue.text: Almost ahead of schedule after November

indicators.note: after means following, so one piece comes behind the other

blocks.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ahead of schedule means early

explanation.surface: Something that is almost early, coming in after the end of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: November gives N via the radio alphabet, not a month abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are interchangeable adverbs meaning not quite, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Global promise to preserve life, primarily

definitions.note: adjective in the clue; the answer is used attributively, as in a world tour

indicators.note: to preserve is to keep safe inside, so one piece holds another
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: to give your word is to promise
the first letter of life

explanation.surface: An international pledge to protect living things, above all.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of life goes inside WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: World used before a noun, as in world peace, means relating to the whole earth, so global.

clue.text: Brown's legislation upset teachers as a body

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: legislation is law
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's law angered the teaching profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like the former Prime Minister but is the colour. The NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British union.
explanation.definitionFit: Walnut is a mid-brown shade named after the wood and shell of the tree, so it is a kind of brown.

clue.text: Tea display vehicle

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a riot of colour is a vivid display

explanation.surface: A van showing off tea, or a tea stall on wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; a riot here is a lavish show, as in a riot of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of ancient times, which is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Copper added note for receptacles

indicators.note: adding means attaching one thing to the end of another

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A police officer leaves a note about containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' tempts as a British policeman, but it is the metal; 'note' is a postscript, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups are small drinking vessels, which makes them a common example of a receptacle.

clue.text: More than one queen, perhaps, in France on vacation with something to say on stage

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: the outer letters of France
an actor's lines are what they speak on stage

explanation.surface: Royal queens holidaying in France with speeches to deliver in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but a queen is also a female cat; 'perhaps' flags that queens are only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is an adult female cat, so several queens are cats, members of the cat family.

clue.text: Take in most of cuisine before start of lunch

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the final letter is dropped
the start is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: cuisine is food
the first letter of lunch

explanation.surface: Eating most of a dish before lunch has properly begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like eating, which suits the surface, but it means to deceive. FOOD loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is an idiom for deceiving or tricking them, which is what a fool-er does.

clue.text: Noisy mass on supporting structure

indicators.note: noisy points to sound, so the words are taken as they are spoken

blocks.note: a pile is a mass of things, and 'on' is kept

explanation.surface: A loud crowd climbing onto a scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile on' spoken quickly matches the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel tower that holds up power lines, so it is a supporting structure.

clue.text: Game note for deep-fried food

blocks.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A game ticket swapped for fried snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the seventh note in do-re-mi, also spelt ti.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small breaded roll of mashed potato or meat cooked in hot oil until crisp.
